key_insight: No single 3D multimodal registration method was robust across anatomies and modalities; higher overlap scores did not reliably mean better global correspondence.
engineering_relevance: For clinical image-guided workflows, this benchmark shows that registration systems should be validated with both geometric and image-based metrics before deployment.
method: Benchmarked intra-patient 3D deformable multimodal registration on three datasets spanning different anatomies and difficulty levels.
Compared classical optimization-based methods with modern learning-based approaches, including deep learning and foundation models.
Evaluated with complementary metrics: DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC to capture overlap, boundary error, and structural similarity.
evidence_signal: Across synthetic and real clinical scenarios, learning-based methods performed best on large synthetic benchmarks, but gains were limited in real pelvic registration and metrics often disagreed.
watch_item: Methods that maximize label overlap can degrade outside segmented regions, so anatomy-guided models need careful assessment for global deformation quality.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
